newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHER QUICKEST IN FIRST MONZA PRACTICE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHER QUICKEST IN FIRST MONZA PRACTICE.

text.p: Double world champion Michael Schumacher picked up where he left off at the Belgian Grand Prix 12 days ago by dominating Friday's opening practice session for Sunday's Italian Grand Prix.

With a typically-flamboyant performance for Ferrari in front of packed stands filled with flag-waving Italians, the German gave a clear indication of his desire to gain his first victory on Italian soil in Sunday's 53-lap race.
His effort also proved he was capable of upsetting the showdown in the drivers' championship between leader Damon Hill of Britain and Hill's Williams team-mate Jacques Villeneuve of Canada.

Hill, dropped for 1997 by Williams since the last Grand Prix outing at Belgium in favour of German Heinz-Harald Frentzen, leads the title race by 13 points and needs a victory, with Villeneuve outside the top three, to claim his first drivers' crown.

But on Friday, Hill could only manage the seventh-fastest time, two places down on Villeneuve and more than 1.3 seconds slower than Schumacher, who delighted Ferrari fans at the fast Monza track through the old parkland circuit north of Milan.

Schumacher's fastest time of one minute and 24.399 seconds was well clear of the best lap-time of both the second-fastest man, Finland's Mika Hakkinen in a McLaren, and Austrian Gerhard Berger, who was third-fastest for Benetton.
Briton Eddie Irvine in the second Ferrari was fourth-quickest -- maintaining a tradition of Ferrari drivers performing well on the opening day of the Monza weekend.
Frentzen was eighth-fastest in his Sauber, immediately behind Hill in the times.
Schumacher was given a rousing reception for his efforts by the Ferrari fans.
"Things went quite well...better than I expected," he said. "The car is fine although there are still a few small problems which I am sure we can solve before tomorrow's qualifying session.

"It is difficult to know if things will be the same or if the opposition will be more competitive tomorrow. But the work carried out here at Monza in the last few weeks has allowed us to get on the right track straight away."

Ferrari's sporting director Jean Todt was equally happy. "This was a good day for us," he said. "Our cars performed strongly, Michael set the quickest time on old tyres and Eddie is fourth despite running into traffic.
"Above all, Schumacher found the car to be well-balanced and I think we can look forward to a good qualifying session."

Hill remained confident despite his time. "I'm very pleased today," he insisted. "I've worked on a set-up and I'm very, very confident. I have absolute confidence in the team's ability to give me as much chance as I need to win the championship."
Hill said he had not used new tyres and his time was not representative of his true potential.
"It is going to be a very close session tomorrow and one of the best we are going to see all season."
